headline: NO published KILL is overturned. The three killed cells whose control run reproduces their published numbers EXACTLY all hold at slippage=0.01. Separately, the harness was found to be NON-MONOTONIC in slippage (a real bug), which invalidates the premise that the 0.02 default was uniformly 2x pessimistic.

population_correction.work_order_claim: 255 call sites, ~241 studies ran on the 2x-pessimistic default
why_the_claim_was_too_high: the raw grep counted .claude/worktrees copies of the same files
it counted imports, defs, docstrings and comment text as call sites
it equated CALL SITES with STUDIES -- many scripts hold several call sites, and most call sites live in scripts that never published a verdict

arms.CONTROL_002: slippage forced to 0.02 on every simulator entry point
arms.TREATMENT_001: slippage forced to 0.01, identical population and code path
arms.method: the function object is wrapped and the kwarg injected before the target script imports it; for the 2 scripts that import and pass the module CONSTANTS explicitly, the constants themselves are rebound pre-import. No repo file edited.
arms.write_sandbox: all writes under analysis/, automation/, strategy/, journal/ redirected to a scratch mirror; verified afterwards that all 47 target artifacts retain their pre-run mtimes

TIER_A_killed_cells_that_reproduce_exact.published: n=10, v1 WR 0.30 / P&L $2.70, v2 WR 0.90 / P&L $272.80, gate_pass false, verdict FAIL
TIER_A_killed_cells_that_reproduce_exact.control_002: reproduced EXACTLY (after reconstructing the rotted input population)
TIER_A_killed_cells_that_reproduce_exact.why: the gate is `wr >= 0.50 in BOTH variants`. Friction moves dollars, not the sign of a trade, so the win rate is untouched. The cell was killed on WIN RATE, which this change cannot address.

TIER_A_killed_cells_that_reproduce_exact.verdict_at_001: 'No TP1 value rescues NLWB to positive' -- unchanged

why_kills_were_never_likely_to_move.the_decisive_one: RANDOM_NULL (6 cells) is mathematically invariant to this change -- the null is simulated under the SAME slippage, so both arms shift together and the DIFFERENCE the gate tests is unchanged. Those 6 can never be rescued by re-baselining friction.
why_kills_were_never_likely_to_move.others_invariant: truncation artifact, frequency floor, look-ahead/coverage, edge_capture (OP-16)
why_kills_were_never_likely_to_move.partially_sensitive: concentration / positive-quarters -- these are RATIOS and marginal quarter signs, so a uniform shift can move them; they are the main source of the sub-cell sign flips below

FINDING_1_harness_is_non_monotonic_in_sl.severity: HIGH -- this is a real bug and it is worth more than the re-baseline
FINDING_1_harness_is_non_monotonic_in_sl.claim: Lowering slippage makes some cells WORSE, which is impossible for a well-formed fill model.
FINDING_1_harness_is_non_monotonic_in_sl.root_cause: Two exit paths fill at an exact price with NO exit_slippage while every market exit pays it: (a) the TP1 premium fallback at entry*(1+tp1_pct) -- defensible, a limit order fills at its limit; (b) the runner stop INCLUDING the post-TP1 breakeven stop -- NOT defensible, a stop executes at market.
FINDING_1_harness_is_non_monotonic_in_sl.arithmetic_proof: For a TP1-limit + BE-runner trade, P&L = tp1_premium_pct * entry_fill * tp1_qty * 100 -- strictly proportional to an entry fill that INCLUDES entry slippage. With TP1_PREMIUM_PCT=0.30, TP1_QTY_FRACTION=2/3, qty=3 -> tp1_qty=2, halving slippage predicts exactly 0.30*0.01*2*100 = $0.60 WORSE per trade. Observed: -$0.60 on EVERY TP1_THEN_RUNNER_RIBBON trade in v14e_ampm_real_fills.
FINDING_1_harness_is_non_monotonic_in_sl.who_it_bites_hardest: EXIT-TUNING sweeps, whose whole purpose is choosing exit parameters. sweep_regime_chandelier is 24/24 cells WORSE at lower slippage; sweep_timecond_exit 23/44; sweep_watcher_exits 20/114; sweep_lunch_trough_gate 8/23.
FINDING_1_harness_is_non_monotonic_in_sl.consequence_for_the_premise: The 0.02 default was NOT uniformly pessimistic. It overstated entry cost and market exits but INFLATED %-target winners and gave every stop a free fill. The SIGN of the bias depends on each cell's exit mix, so there is no single 'dollars of baked-in pessimism' number and none is reported.
FINDING_1_harness_is_non_monotonic_in_sl.evidence_of_exit_mix_dependence: same script, same trades, v14e_chart_stop_research: the premium-stop arm moved +$39.60 while the market-exit arm moved +$548.80 -- a 14x difference from exit mix alone.
FINDING_1_harness_is_non_monotonic_in_sl.recommended_fix: apply exit_slippage to the runner-stop fills in both affected modules, then add a vary-and-assert guard to backtest/tests/test_graduated_guards.py. NOT done here -- it changes every backtest result and needs its own prereg.

FINDING_2_deltas_are_path_divergence_not.severity: HIGH -- this is why no sign flip in this study is trustworthy evidence
FINDING_2_deltas_are_path_divergence_not.claim: Most measured cell deltas are dominated by slippage-induced EXIT RECLASSIFICATION, not by the friction change itself.
FINDING_2_deltas_are_path_divergence_not.arithmetic_bound: the direct friction effect is bounded at $0.02/share * 100 * qty = ~$6/trade at qty=3. Deltas far exceeding that bound cannot be friction.
FINDING_2_deltas_are_path_divergence_not.worked_example: _recency_stop_variant_ab ITM-2 / chartstop-only / recent_window: n=11 in BOTH arms, yet exp_per_trade went -$39.60 -> +$41.04 (+$80.64/trade, a $887 swing). The exit mix changed: EXIT_ALL_LEVEL_STOP 3->2, TP1_THEN_RUNNER_RIBBON 1->2. ONE trade's exit path flipped and carried the entire cell.
FINDING_2_deltas_are_path_divergence_not.mechanism: a 1c cheaper entry lowers the stop level; on a 5-MINUTE-bar option cache that can move the breach across a bar boundary so a different exit fires first. Already a documented limitation (OPTION-BAR-RESOLUTION-BIAS-2026-08-02, $1,821.75 aggregate swing).
FINDING_2_deltas_are_path_divergence_not.prevalence: 70 of 129 exit-mix distributions (54.3%) changed between arms, across 8 of the 9 scripts that report one.
FINDING_2_deltas_are_path_divergence_not.conclusion: sign flips produced by this study are NOT evidence about any cell's true edge.

sign_flips.what_they_are: almost entirely SWEEP-GRID sub-cells and slices (by_quarter, by_side, by_regime, exit_mini_sweeps[N], all_cells[N], grid[N]) in studies carrying 80-1126 P&L cells each. With that many cells, a uniform shift crossing zero somewhere is arithmetically guaranteed -- it is the multiple-comparisons surface these studies' own gates exist to defend against (anti-pattern 2.10).
headline_metric_flips_worth_naming: _b6_turn_of_month_drift primary_per_trade -12.85 -> +0.88 (cell died on 5/8 gates incl. random-null and concentration; both invariant or barely moved, so the kill stands)
sign_flips.ruling: NONE is nominated for re-validation. Per the frozen prereg a nomination requires the control to reproduce the published numbers (these are all DIFFERS or worse), n>=15, a non-marginal clearance of the ORIGINAL kill threshold, and drop-best survival. None qualifies, and FINDING_2 independently disqualifies flips driven by path divergence.

aggregate_pessimism_deliberately_NOT_qua.why: a naive sum over all P&L keys gives $1,377,291.71, which is meaningless -- it double-counts nested keys and sums across hundreds of mutually exclusive sweep-grid cells that were never a portfolio. Reporting it would be a fabricated headline.
what_can_honestly_be_said: the DIRECT friction effect is ~$0.02/contract/round-trip, i.e. ~$6/trade at qty=3, and only on market-priced exits
on proportional exits (premium stop, %-target TP1) the effect is scaled down by the stop/target percentage, and on stop fills it is currently ZERO because of FINDING_1
the three Tier-A killed cells moved +$14.60, +$80 and +$80 -- 5-10% of their deficits

reasons.input rot (dominant): automation/state/watcher-observations.jsonl is a ROLLING file rotated into archive/ by heal-engine.ps1 past 1MB; it now holds ONE day. Studies keyed on it match zero rows, exit 0, and emit a real-looking verdict at n=0. 7,681 rows over 376 dates were recovered from the archives, which reproduced orb_real_fills EXACTLY -- but the reconstruction is a SUPERSET (v14e re-runs n=132 vs published 100), so it validates the method without restoring most published snapshots.
reasons.OPRA cache-edge guard (2 scripts): _web_vwap_cont_late_entry_theta_cliff and _wp5_strike_ab assert `fill date <= cache edge 2026-05-29`; the SPY feed has since extended past it. Their guard fired correctly. Not re-runnable without editing a hardcoded constant (out of scope).
reasons.harness gap (1 script): lbfs_shadow_revalidation writes via an unguarded Path.open; it failed CLOSED (no repo write) and ran fine in the reconstructed-input arm.
reasons.different exit engine (1 script): recency_check routes its live-path replay through lib/exit_manager_walk.walk_exit_manager, not simulate_trade_real (which it imports for a legacy path only). walk_exit_manager carries its OWN fill model, so the simulator patch legitimately does not reach it. Not a bug.
reasons.argparse-gated writers (12 scripts): only emit an artifact when given --out; re-run separately with the flag and included in the results above.

validity_controls_run.write_sandbox_verified: all 47 target artifacts retain pre-run mtimes; the 3 files that did change were written by concurrent scheduled tasks (recency_check writes via the PATCHED Path.write_text, and this session's run was ~1h earlier)
validity_controls_run.patch_binds_C14_vary_and_assert: confirmed; the 3 initial PATCH_DID_NOT_BIND cases were diagnosed rather than reported as 'no effect' -- 2 were explicit-constant callers (fixed by rebinding the constants; both then reproduced and held) and 1 uses a different exit engine
validity_controls_run.rng_noise_floor: 0 differing numeric keys across identical-slippage replicates (339 keys on _sel_vwap_sizing; 0 on every gated script measured). The 10 scripts with unseeded randomness do not have it reach their reported outputs.
validity_controls_run.arms_symmetric: 78 scripts each, 74 OK / 4 ERROR in both arms

actions_taken: NONE beyond publishing. No cell re-armed, no kill reversed, no live config touched, module defaults NOT changed (explicitly out of scope per the work order).
recommended_next: Fix the runner-stop slippage in simulator_real.py + simulator_real_trailing.py under its own prereg, then add a monotonicity vary-and-assert guard. This blocks a clean re-baseline until done.
Re-baseline the module defaults to 0.01 ONLY AFTER that fix, otherwise the re-baseline bakes in the non-monotonicity.
Make studies snapshot their input population (or an input hash + row count) into their own artifact, and treat n==0 as NO_RESULT rather than a verdict.
